evals.prompt: Set up Pipa for my business. I do brand strategy for early-stage founders and prefer concise async updates.
evals.expected_output: Checks the global profile, gets setup acceptance, runs read-only preflight, asks only missing core questions one at a time, and saves incremental profile state before connector review and completion.
assertions: Does it use `~/.pipa/profile.md` as the setup state and business-context source of truth?
Does it ask only what the user does, who they help or work with, and how they like to work, one at a time and without repeating supplied answers?
Does it save answered or skipped fields incrementally with `setup_status: incomplete`, then mark the profile complete after connector review?

evals.prompt: Set up Pipa. My global Pipa profile already says setup_status: complete.
evals.expected_output: Routes to profile review or update rather than restarting first-time questions.
assertions: Does it treat the completed profile marker as deterministic completion?
Does it update only requested fields while preserving `setup_status: complete` and skip connector review unless requested?
Does it avoid inferring setup state from memory or project files?

evals.prompt: Resume Pipa setup. The profile is incomplete, and it already records what I do and who I help.
evals.expected_output: Preserves confirmed answers and resumes at how the user likes to work.
assertions: Does it resume at the first unanswered core question?
Does it preserve rather than re-ask or overwrite confirmed facts?
Does it keep setup incomplete until connector review finishes?

evals.prompt: Resume Pipa setup. The profile is incomplete, but all three core questions are already answered or skipped.
evals.expected_output: Resumes at connector review without repeating questions or marking setup complete before review finishes.
assertions: Does it preserve all confirmed or skipped profile fields?
Does it resume directly at relevant connector review without re-asking core questions?
Does it wait until connector review finishes before marking setup complete?

evals.prompt: Set up Pipa, but I want to skip the profile questions and I do not want to connect tools right now.
evals.expected_output: Allows every biographical question and connector setup to be declined while still completing the profile with explicit skipped fields.
assertions: Does it allow all three core questions to be skipped?
Does it allow connector setup to be declined without trapping the user?
Does it mark setup complete after connector review and summarize skipped or unknown state honestly?

evals.prompt: During Pipa setup, connect whichever tools you think I need.
evals.expected_output: Uses profile context to recommend relevant tools, discovers support and status first, and asks before starting authorization.
assertions: Does it recommend only connections relevant to the requested help?
Does it discover connection support and current status before availability claims?
Does it ask before OAuth and verify successful connections with a read-only check rather than a write?

evals.prompt: Set up Pipa and use https://example.com to help draft my business profile.
evals.expected_output: Offers a read-only best-effort website read and uses only supported public facts while still asking the core questions.
assertions: Does it treat website assistance as optional and read-only?
Does it confirm and save only supported facts under optional website context without overwriting user-provided content?
Does it avoid enrichment services, email reverse lookup, or invented positioning?

evals.prompt: I have never set up Pipa and there is no profile, but first help me plan this urgent client delivery.
evals.expected_output: Routes the concrete request to define work without forcing setup, with at most a soft setup next step afterward.
assertions: Does it avoid forcing setup ahead of concrete work?
Does it avoid treating absent project context as a prerequisite?
Does any setup mention remain a soft, non-blocking next step?

evals.prompt: Finish setting up Pipa and create a daily brief automation while you are there.
evals.expected_output: Completes setup without creating automation and explicitly defers Daily Brief behavior to its separate follow-up work.
assertions: Does it avoid creating tasks, reminders, automations, triggers, or recurring workflows during setup?
Does it keep Daily Brief outside first-time setup?
Does it defer Daily Brief to its separate follow-up rather than inventing a scheduled-automation route?

evals.prompt: Not now. Skip Pipa setup and help me with my actual work instead.
evals.expected_output: Accepts the decline, performs no setup preflight, and continues with the concrete work route.
assertions: Does it avoid reading memory or connected-tool status for setup after setup is declined?
Does it avoid creating or changing `~/.pipa/profile.md`?
Does it continue with the user's concrete work without another setup question?

evals.prompt: Finish Pipa setup. The tool I need is not supported by the available connector discovery results.
evals.expected_output: Reports the connector as unavailable, preserves captured profile facts, and completes setup without claiming support.
assertions: Does it ground unavailability in connector discovery results?
Does it preserve the profile and avoid requesting credentials or inventing an auth path?
Does it complete setup with connection state `unavailable`?

evals.prompt: Finish Pipa setup. I approved the connector, but its smallest read-only verification failed.
evals.expected_output: Reports failed verification without retrying through a write, preserves profile facts, and still completes setup.
assertions: Does it report the failed read-only verification honestly?
Does it avoid testing the connection with a write action?
Does it preserve the profile and complete setup with connection state `failed`?

evals.prompt: My Pipa profile is complete. Review which connectors are relevant now, but do not change my profile fields.
evals.expected_output: Reviews relevant connectors without restarting setup or changing completed profile content.
assertions: Does it preserve `setup_status: complete` and all existing profile fields?
Does it run connector review because the user explicitly requested it?
Does it avoid re-asking the three first-time setup questions?
